When Rachel got to work that morning, she found the parking lot spot reserved for the old town tree sign vacant; someone had been quick to remove it after the demolition crew left. That's when the sense of suffocating dread wrapped itself around her chest like a shroud... "What am I going to tell Mrs. Jenkins?"

Her boss stood nearby, scrutinizing Rachel from under knitted brows as she hesitated in front of their usually chatty door at the front desk. Today it felt oppressive and empty.

"How...what happened to our park sign?" Rachel stammered awkwardly when Mrs. Jenkins arrived and gave a faint sniff – the morning air clotted with dismay like she sensed it was contagious around here...

"Tree's still gone, you see," Mrs. Jenkins droned on mechanically about council approval paperwork - "and I've received a message to keep this quiet until further notice..." Rachel's heart grew colder inside itself now.

Rachel didn't get the feeling that anyone had been prepared for something like this to happen – so quietly...

topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
story:
When she stumbled awake to an email from her mom, Sophia could tell at once it was some bad news. The subject line screamed of bureaucratic horrors: RELOCATION OF OLD TOWN TREE NOW CONFIRMED.

The rest didn't read much better: "Some new developer had moved in and convinced the town that 'modernization' needed taking priority over preserving green spaces..."

"Who let them do this to our city?" Sophia asked aloud, crumpling up a pillow behind her head as it came crushing down on her now-dodgy gut. The weight made every breath feel harder than ever after all these years, yet – somehow...this...kept getting worse.

The screen binged out a series of sadistic images of the cleared site - some empty lot where once she had played carefree hours watching life unfurl under those towering branches... Her own thoughts felt broken into millions of brittle slivers. "Must have been someone new in office," her brain spat silently...

But, no – couldn't be that – everyone knew about the promises made on sacred grounds - the history she grew up listening to with each passing night...

topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
story:
For weeks after word got out about how the old town tree died under some developer's bulldozer blade, Jesse kept having these awful, dark dreams in which he relived all of his family's sad memories. Like an old ache, it would hurt more than even thinking was worth; and he'd wake right up, expecting to see the beautiful, tall shade standing before him – but none of those things were there anymore.

He'd take one good look at himself every morning - or try to: in some moments of weakness Jesse felt as if his heart had given away too soon to be saved... This pain only hurt harder with time. As it usually did, the anger got more intense now when he walked out into sunlight and spotted these city workers busy rearranging things about town.

In those instances - just walking out here among all this empty space - things felt really hard: it was so much easier staying away from anything reminding him of that tree his family had once loved...

He'd started to notice more of the people with angry looks crossing paths on sidewalks now...
